title: Layer rail and hotkeys
kicker: Session and shell · how you play
hook: The **layer rail** is the shared set of menus and hotkeys — Creatures, Fusion, Expeditions, and the rest — that open over whatever stage you are on.

blindSpots.meaning: Not a train. The fixed list of layers and keys available from any stage.
A panel drawn over the current stage. Closing it returns you exactly where you were.
One letter (or Esc) that opens that layer. Same letter on Sanctum, lawn, or map.
Layers can pile up. Esc closes the top one; on an empty stack, Esc opens System.

alsoTrue: Locked layers stay visible and say what unlocks them — see [unlock beats](unlock-beats).
You are usually standing in the [Sanctum](sanctum) when you first learn the rail.

sections.title: The keys
sections.intro: Memorize the verb, not a different shortcut per screen:

rows: Close top layer; on empty stack → System

sections.note: Travel to the world map is `M` — that changes stage, it is not a layer on the rail.

sections.title: How it feels
paras: Open Creatures mid-hall, check a demon, close — you are still in the Sanctum.
The same C works if you later open the rail from another stage. You do not learn a second UI language.
diagram: [ layer over the stage ]  --Esc-->  back to stage

sections.title: What the rail is not
paras: It is not a website sidebar of separate pages you navigate away to.
It is not the lawn game’s own pause menu — that is the host pack. This rail is Rise of Summoner’s control-room chrome.

doSteps: In the Sanctum, press `C` — Creatures should open over the hall.
Press Esc (or the close control) and confirm you are still in the Sanctum.
Press `?` or open System and confirm the keymap matches this table.
doNote: Stop when one key feels global. Next: [unlock beats](unlock-beats) so locked entries make sense.

mixUps.q: Why can’t I open Relics yet?
mixUps.a: It unlocks when you hold your first item. The entry should say so — see [unlock beats](unlock-beats).

mixUps.q: Is Fusion the host game’s name?
mixUps.a: No. On the rail, Fusion (`F`) is specimen merge. The host pack is Plants vs. Zombies: Fusion.

mixUps.q: Does Esc always quit the game?
mixUps.a: No. Esc closes the top layer first. Only on an empty stack does it open System (quit lives there).
M travels to the world map — a stage change, not a layer.

mixUps.q: Do keys change on the lawn stage?
mixUps.a: No. Same rail letters. That is the point of one rail.
